texts.error.dlc_refused: The DLC %1 cannot go on the memory stick: %2. It has to be a zip of the memory stick, as Export Save Data writes it, or of the folders to put under %3.
texts.error.no_vulkan_bridge: The renderer setting is vulkan-hw, and no Vulkan was handed over (this computer may have no Vulkan driver, or this Chimera is older than its Vulkan bridge).
texts.error.no_vulkan_build: The renderer setting is vulkan-hw, and this build has no Vulkan renderer.
texts.error.not_started: PPSSPP could not start the machine.
texts.error.save_missing: The save data %1 is not there.
texts.error.save_refused: The save data %1 cannot go on the memory stick: %2. It has to be a zip of the memory stick, as Export Save Data writes it, or of the folders to put under %3.
texts.error.vulkan_not_started: The Vulkan renderer could not start: %1
texts.error.zip_entry: an entry of it could not be read
texts.error.zip_outside: it holds '%1', which is outside the memory stick
texts.firmware.jpn0_pgf.about: The console's Japanese font. Copy it from your own console (folder flash0:/font). A real copy is exactly 1581700 bytes, and a file with that size and the listed hash is shown as ok. The listed hash is of the file in Sony's last official firmware (6.61). Any readable file you choose is used, including a replacement font of your own. Such a file is shown as custom or unrecognised and is not refused, and a movie records its hash. The file is optional. Without it the core uses the free replacement font included in the package, which has different character shapes and sizes. That is a different machine, and a movie records which one was used.

texts.setting.buttonpreference.about: Which button the system uses to confirm: Circle on Japanese consoles and Cross elsewhere. Games read it to arrange their menus.
texts.setting.cpuclock.about: Fixes the processor's speed at this many MHz. 0 leaves the speed to the game (the console starts at 222 MHz and a game can raise it to 333). A lower or higher speed changes the timing, so this is part of the machine.
texts.setting.cpucore.about: How the PSP's MIPS processor is emulated. The x86 JIT is the default. It is much faster and runs inside the sandbox like everything else, and the code it produces is saved in savestates. The IR interpreter is slower and is the fallback. The two can behave differently in rare cases, so this is part of the machine and a movie records it.
texts.setting.dateformat.about: The console's date format setting, which games read to show dates.
texts.setting.daylightsavings.about: The console's daylight-saving setting, which games can read.
texts.setting.encryptsave.about: Encrypts save data the way a real console does. With it off the saves can be read and edited, and they are no longer in the form a real console writes.
texts.setting.firmwareversion.about: The system software version that games see (660 means 6.60). Some games check it at start-up.
texts.setting.fontsource.about: 'bundled' uses the free replacement fonts included in the package. No firmware is needed, and the characters have different shapes and sizes than on a real console. 'sony' uses the console's own fonts from flash0. Each font file is then asked for on the wizard's firmware page, and you supply your own copies.
texts.setting.funcreplacements.about: Replaces some well-known routines in games (memory copying and similar) with fast built-in versions. On is PPSSPP's default. Off is closer to the timing of a real console.
texts.setting.iotiming.about: How long reading and writing the disc and the memory stick takes. 'fast' finishes quickly, 'simulated' takes realistic times and 'umd-slow' imitates a slow UMD drive. PPSSPP also has a mode that follows your computer's clock. It is not offered, because it would differ on every run.
texts.setting.language.about: The console's system language. Games read it at start-up to choose their language, so it is part of the machine.
texts.setting.macaddress.about: The console's wireless network address, written as XX:XX:XX:XX:XX:XX. Games read it to identify the console, and some take their random numbers from it.
texts.setting.nickname.about: The owner's name in the console's settings. Games read it for save files and default player names.
texts.setting.parentallevel.about: The console's parental-control level (0 to 11). Some games limit their content by it.
texts.setting.pspmodel.about: Which model this is. The PSP-2000 (Slim) has 64 MB of memory and the PSP-1000 has 32 MB. A few games use the extra memory. It is part of the machine, so changing it restarts the core and a movie records it.
texts.setting.renderer.about: Which renderer draws the picture. 'software' is PPSSPP's software renderer and the default. It runs completely inside the core on the processor, so the picture is the same on every computer that plays the movie. 'vulkan-hw' is PPSSPP's Vulkan renderer drawing on your computer's graphics card. Its picture comes from a driver that is outside the core and outside the savestate, and it differs between computers; a movie recorded with it records that a graphics card drew the picture. It draws at the PSP's own resolution, 480x272. It has nothing to fall back on: it needs a graphics driver that has Vulkan and a Chimera that hands Vulkan to cores, and without either the project does not start and says why. The renderer is part of the machine: with some games the two do not take the same time to draw, and the game then runs differently (Crash Tag Team Racing's memory differs between them from the first seconds). So choose it when you create the project; a movie made with one may not play back with the other. With 'vulkan-hw' the game itself still runs the same on every computer - only the picture depends on the graphics card.
texts.setting.rtcbase.about: The console's date and time at power-on, written as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS. Games read the clock for the dates of save files, for daily events and for content that depends on the date. From this start the clock advances with the emulated console and never with your computer's clock. A value that cannot be read is replaced by the default.
texts.setting.timeformat.about: The console's time format setting, which games read to show times.
texts.setting.timezone.about: The console's time zone as a difference from UTC in minutes (-720 to 840). Games read it together with the clock.
texts.slot.disc.help: The PSP game. It can be a UMD dump (.iso, or compressed .cso) or homebrew (an EBOOT .pbp, or a plain .prx or .elf).
texts.slot.dlc.help: Downloadable content. It is either a zip of the game's DLC folder as it is on a memory stick (for example ULUS10336, with the EDAT files and PARAM.PBP inside), which is put under PSP/GAME, or a zip of a whole memory stick, whose PSP/ folders are put where they belong. It is unpacked onto the memory stick before the machine starts, and its hash is recorded like the save data's. Several zips can be given.
texts.slot.savedata.help: What is already saved on the memory stick when the PSP starts. It is either the zip that Emulator > Export Save Data... writes, used as it is, or a zip of save folders copied from a memory stick (for example ULUS10041DATA00, with its PARAM.SFO, icons and the game's files), which are put under PSP/SAVEDATA. The zip is unpacked onto the memory stick before the machine starts. The file is never changed. The project and the movie record exactly which file it was, so a run that starts from a saved game can be played back by anyone who has the same file. Leave this empty and the memory stick has no saves.
